what_its_for: This medicine is used to relieve headaches, including migraines, and tension headaches. It combines two pain relievers (acetaminophen and aspirin) with caffeine, which helps boost the pain-relieving effects. It may also be used for minor aches and pains such as muscle aches, toothaches, and menstrual cramps.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with a full glass of water (8 ounces). You may take it with food or milk if it upsets your stomach. Do not crush or chew tablets — swallow them whole. Do not take more than the recommended dose. Avoid lying down for at least 10 minutes after taking this medicine.
dosing: Adults and children 12 years and older: Take 2 tablets every 6 hours as needed. Do not take more than 8 tablets (4 doses) in 24 hours unless directed by your doctor. Do not use for more than 10 days in a row for pain, or more than 3 days in a row for fever, without talking to your doctor. Children under 12 years: Do NOT use this medicine — ask your doctor for a safe alternative.
missed_dose: This medicine is usually taken only when needed for pain, so a regular dosing schedule may not apply. If you are on a scheduled dose and miss it, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never double up doses to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package. Safely dispose of any unused or expired medicine through a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine — it increases your risk of stomach bleeding and liver damage. Avoid taking other products that also contain acetaminophen (such as cold medicines, sleep aids, or other pain relievers) to prevent accidentally taking too much. Avoid caffeine from other sources like coffee, tea, energy drinks, or soda, as too much caffeine can cause nervousness, rapid heartbeat, or trouble sleeping. Do not take this medicine if you are allergic to aspirin or NSAIDs. Avoid taking on an empty stomach if you have a sensitive stomach. Do not give aspirin-containing products to children or teenagers with flu symptoms or chickenpox due to the risk of Reye's syndrome, a rare but serious condition.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience: ringing in your ears or hearing loss, stomach pain, black or bloody stools, vomiting blood or material that looks like coffee grounds, yellowing of the skin or eyes (signs of liver problems), allergic reactions such as hives, rash, swelling of the face or throat, difficulty breathing, chest pain, rapid or irregular heartbeat, severe dizziness, or if your headache is the 'worst headache of your life' or is different from your usual headaches. Also call your doctor if your pain does not improve after 10 days, gets worse, or if you develop a fever lasting more than 3 days.
when_it_works: This medicine usually starts to relieve pain within 30 minutes to 1 hour after taking it. For best results with migraines, take it at the first sign of a headache before the pain gets worse.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant. Aspirin is generally not recommended during pregnancy, especially in the last 3 months. Breastfeeding: Consult your doctor before use, as aspirin and caffeine can pass into breast milk. Older adults (65+): Use with caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to stomach bleeding and kidney effects. People with certain health conditions should talk to their doctor before use, including those with liver disease, kidney disease, stomach ulcers, bleeding disorders, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma, or a history of stroke. People who drink 3 or more alcoholic drinks per day should ask their doctor before using this medicine.
